name: The Church Fathers
dom: Patristic theology; doctrine; ecclesiastical authority
note: Collective hub for the Patristic Doctors and Apostolic Fathers (c. 1st-8th c.); a standard category in Christian tradition (Quasten's Patrology), not a single historical person.

name: Augustine of Hippo
dom: Grace; original sin; Trinitarian theology; philosophy of history
note: Bishop of Hippo (354-430), one of the four Latin Doctors; attested by his own Confessions and City of God and by Possidius's Vita.

name: Jerome of Stridon
dom: Scripture translation (Vulgate); biblical exegesis; asceticism
note: Priest and scholar (c. 347-420), one of the four Latin Doctors; attested by his own letters and prefaces and by Gennadius.

name: Ambrose of Milan
dom: Hymnody; ecclesiology; anti-Arian polemic; episcopal authority
note: Bishop of Milan (c. 339-397), one of the four Latin Doctors; baptizer of Augustine, attested by Paulinus's Vita.

name: Gregory the Great
dom: Pastoral theology; liturgy; monasticism; mission
note: Pope Gregory I (c. 540-604), one of the four Latin Doctors; attested by his own letters, Dialogues, and Pastoral Rule.

name: Origen of Alexandria
dom: Biblical exegesis; allegory; speculative theology; the Hexapla
note: Alexandrian exegete (c. 184-253); foundational but later partly condemned, attested by Eusebius's Ecclesiastical History and his own surviving works.

name: Irenaeus of Lyons
dom: Anti-Gnostic polemic; apostolic succession; recapitulation theology
note: Bishop of Lyons (c. 130-202); author of Against Heresies, attested by that work and by Eusebius.

name: Tertullian
dom: Latin theological vocabulary (Trinitas); apologetics; rigorism
note: Carthaginian writer (c. 155-220), first major Latin Christian author; later a Montanist, attested by his own corpus and by Jerome.

name: Cyprian of Carthage
dom: Ecclesiology; unity of the Church; the lapsed; martyrdom
note: Bishop of Carthage (c. 210-258), martyr; attested by his own letters and treatises and by the Acta proconsularia.

name: Justin Martyr
dom: Apologetics; the Logos doctrine; engagement with philosophy
note: Greek apologist (c. 100-165), martyr; attested by his First and Second Apologies, the Dialogue with Trypho, and the Acts of his martyrdom.

name: Clement of Alexandria
dom: Christian philosophy; catechesis; the true gnosis
note: Titus Flavius Clemens (c. 150-215), head of the Alexandrian catechetical school; attested by his Protrepticus, Paedagogus, and Stromata and by Eusebius.

name: Clement of Rome
dom: Church order; concord; early Roman primacy
note: Bishop of Rome (late 1st c.), an Apostolic Father; attested chiefly by the First Epistle of Clement (1 Clement) and by later episcopal lists.

name: Ignatius of Antioch
dom: Episcopacy; Eucharist; martyrdom; church unity
note: Bishop of Antioch (d. c. 108), an Apostolic Father and martyr; attested by his seven authentic letters written en route to martyrdom in Rome.

name: Polycarp of Smyrna
dom: Apostolic transmission; martyrdom; pastoral exhortation
note: Bishop of Smyrna (c. 69-155), an Apostolic Father, disciple of John; attested by his Letter to the Philippians and the Martyrdom of Polycarp.

name: Hilary of Poitiers
dom: Anti-Arian Trinitarian theology; Latin defense of Nicaea
note: Bishop of Poitiers (c. 310-367), Doctor of the Church, called 'the Athanasius of the West'; attested by his De Trinitate and by Jerome.

name: Leo the Great
dom: Christology (the Tome); papal primacy; preaching
note: Pope Leo I (c. 400-461), Doctor of the Church; his Tome shaped the Council of Chalcedon (451), attested by his letters and sermons.

name: John of Damascus
dom: Dogmatic synthesis; defense of icons; systematics
note: Damascene monk and theologian (c. 675-749), Doctor of the Church, traditionally the last of the Greek Fathers; author of the Fount of Knowledge and the Apologies against the iconoclasts.

name: Bede the Venerable
dom: Ecclesiastical history; exegesis; chronology (computus)
note: Northumbrian monk (c. 673-735), Doctor of the Church; author of the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, attested by his own works and autobiographical note.

name: Isidore of Seville
dom: Encyclopedic learning (Etymologiae); transmission of patristic heritage
note: Bishop of Seville (c. 560-636), Doctor of the Church, often called the last of the Latin Fathers; author of the Etymologiae.

name: Gregory of Nyssa
dom: Trinitarian theology; mystical theology; apophaticism
note: Bishop of Nyssa (c. 335-395), one of the three Cappadocian Fathers, younger brother of Basil; attested by his theological and ascetical corpus. Distinct from existing Gregory the Theologian (Nazianzen) and Gregory Palamas in the DB.

name: Cyril of Alexandria
dom: Christology; the Theotokos title; anti-Nestorian polemic
note: Patriarch of Alexandria (c. 376-444), Doctor of the Church; leading figure at the Council of Ephesus (431), attested by his letters and dogmatic works. Distinct from existing Cyril and Methodius in the DB.

name: Maximus the Confessor
dom: Christology (two wills); cosmic theology; the spiritual life
note: Byzantine monk and theologian (c. 580-662), opponent of Monothelitism; attested by his own extensive corpus and the Acts of his trial.
